notes.title: Devblog #4
notes.content:
[p]Hello, [/p][p]some time has passed since our last meeting, and we haven’t been idle. In the past few weeks, a lot has happened in the project, and we’re excited to share with you today a [b]build update[/b]. The version you last saw is now about a month old (07/04/25), and since then, numerous new assets, features, and improvements have been added to further sharpen the gameplay experience.[/p][p][/p][p]Our goal was to integrate the multiplayer mode, significantly enhance the user interface, and provide players with more options during combat to develop the best battle strategy for their inventory. [/p][p][/p][p]Everything you find in this email is part of the build we’ll be showcasing at this year’s Gamescom—perfect for getting an early look at the new features.

[b]From August 20th to 22nd, we will be showcasing SoE at Gamescom Business Area on the SAXONY communal stand.[/b][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45354938/620b06822daef38ec74eda65e72b13b8e4cc5fd6.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The player can now compete against other players in [b]PVP[/b] and attempt to defeat them in combat. If they succeed in reducing the opponent’s health points to zero, the player receives [b]ghost souls[/b]. These can be exchanged at the new Ghost Smith for powerful abilities (for example, it’s possible to steal an item from the PvP opponent). [/p][p][/p][p]In preparation for the duel, during the merchant phase the opponent’s inventory, character, and status values are viewable. In the combat phase, their actions and status values—such as shield and health points—are displayed in real time and enhanced with new VFX.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45354938/61112988c943468555c990a938477bf1132660ee.jpg"][/img][/p][p]There are many new [b]items[/b]. Among them is the new category: "Divine Items". These are very rare but far stronger than legendary items and identifiable by their ominous red coloring. [/p][p][/p][p]You can now also collect items within a round, e.g. from treasure piles, to find gemstones and combine them with rings in the shop. [/p][p][/p][p]Additionally, there is a new category: [b]banners[/b], which grant the player extra bonuses when in range, but at the cost of movement freedom.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45354938/9974f292358d62adfcc544081f444d053e5229a5.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The [b]Skeleton Bomber[/b] carries a barrel on its back. If it is killed, the danger is averted, but if it gets too close to you, the fuse ignites and it explodes.  This explosion can trigger devastating chain reactions. However, with a bit of skill, the Skeleton Bomber can also be used strategically to wipe out entire hordes of enemies. [/p][p][/p][p]Priests come in two variants: one version grants enemies protective armor, identifiable by its metallic appearance and blue glow. The other enhances their speed, identifiable by the green coloring. After casting a spell, all nearby enemies are immediately buffed. So kill the Priest quickly before he turns his allies into powerful threats. [/p][p][/p][p]The [b]Ghost[/b] appears when the opposing player is stronger than you. This further emphasizes their superiority, but at the same time gives you the chance to turn the tables by granting you increased gold income.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45354938/e2e1a6e9d1e1d505a20c840808a2f007d234d5f0.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The [b]Obelisks[/b] grant you powerful bonuses within a radius. Which type of buff it is can be identified by its tip. This allows you, at the expense of other activities and with increased horde danger, to boost specific attributes in order to defeat more enemies with the same build. 

Destroying [b]barrels[/b] opens up new ways to interact with the world. There are three types of barrels: [/p][list][*][p][b]Explosive Barrel:[/b] Works similarly to the Skeleton Bomber and can also trigger devastating chain reactions.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Oil Barrel:[/b] When destroyed, whether by the player or by an explosion, an oil slick spreads out. This can be ignited and deals damage to everything within it as long as it burns. Players and enemies are slowed, and enemies are additionally weakened.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Grass:[/b] Behaves similarly to oil, but remains for the entire round. Grass is created by water released from destroyed [b]water barrels[/b], which can extinguish oil fires.[/p][/*][/list][p] Collecting [b]treasures[/b] is a new way to earn gold. Anything that can be sold can be converted into gold at the push of a button during the shop phase.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45354938/2890394f518b6eb40d5d70f9e7d7e0ed24edcdac.jpg"][/img][/p][p]The [b]lighting[/b] has been overhauled. Shadows are more realistic and softer, sunsets more believable, and ruins spookier yet pleasantly bright so as not to disrupt the flow of gameplay. With the improved lighting, the [b]VFX[/b] now appear far more detailed, and subtle color nuances are easier to discern.  By adjusting contrasts and color values, the look is now much more consistent across a variety of screen types. [/p][p][/p][p][b]Grass[/b] is not only functional but also a visual building block. During a round, as much grass as possible can grow, depending on how much water is available and how much of it is destroyed. [/p][p][/p][p]In the [b]UI[/b], many elements have been harmonized. Placeholders have been replaced with final graphics, and interaction options are now more intuitive and comprehensible. [/p][p][/p][p]Similarly, [b]performance[/b] has been improved despite the new effects, especially in the UI area.[/p][p][/p][p][b]Thank you for reading, we’ll see you at Gamescom![/b][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: Devblog #3
notes.content:
Hey everyone, we’re back again!
Time really flies when you're having fun, it feels like I made the last post just yesterday! Today we've got some updates on previously mentioned topics and, of course, another [b]sneak peek[/b] just for you!

Let’s start by talking about the most important part first. We mentioned the improved [b]onboarding[/b] last time, and we’ve been working on it ever since. Your first contact with the game should feel as amazing as we know it can be, so to ensure that, we’ve put even more effort into it. We’re confident we’re on the right track as we are making progress every single day!

Secondly, we’ve been talking a lot about the [b]look and feel[/b] of the game in recent posts, but we haven’t really delivered on showcasing it, until now. Managing your inventory is a crucial part of the game, so we want it to feel both fun and impactful. Take a look at what we’ve cooked up for our [b]attribute transformation system[/b]!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45354938/34e0cd46e1452c0bcffe32e2e2c97f9ca642e858.gif[/img]
It doesn’t just look pretty, it also has a really cool sound effect! If you want to hear it, feel free to head over to our Twitter page and check it out!

To wrap up today’s dev blog, we want to revisit the setting. We’re heading to Ancient Egypt, where players will face a deadly curse. So far, the gameplay hasn’t fully reflected the hostile environment of our setting, but that’s about to change! We’re thinking [b]sandstorms[/b], [b]falling objects[/b], and other [b]environmental elements[/b] that scream: [i]You are not welcome here![/i]

notes.title: Devblog #2
notes.content:
Hey again, everyone!

We’re back with our second devblog and excited to share what we’ve been working on over the past two weeks, so let's jump right into it and talk about what we promised last time!

We’ve made some great progress on the look and feel of the game! We've added new VFX to make everything feel more satisfying and dynamic, and while it’s already coming together nicely, it’s definitely still a work in progress. There are a ton of ideas floating around for how to make the game really shine, so we’ll be continuing to polish and tweak things as we go.

Last time, we also teased the class system rework, so let’s talk about that! We've been playtesting with four core classes until now: the Mage, the Knight, the Ranger, and the Nobody (yep, that’s actually the name). But we figured you might want even more variety, so we’ve come up with four brand-new classes! Say hello to the [b]Assassin[/b], the [b]Merchant[/b], the [b]Jeweler[/b], and the [b]Gambler[/b]. We’ve got some pretty fun concepts lined up for each of them, but we’ll keep the details under wraps for now.

We also spent some time improving onboarding, which we mentioned needed a bit of love in the last post. We've built a [b]new system to help guide fresh players[/b] more smoothly into the game, now the goal is to make it feel just as awesome as the rest of the experience.


What kind of devblog would this be without at least one sneak peek?  Don’t worry, we’ve got you covered!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45354938/60285a405f1fb55a7f2d13062affe01e08334976.png[/img]
There will be [b]lots[/b] of achievements for you to unlock, each one making you stronger for your journey, as they provide you with skill points. As the skill tree is currently undergoing a reshaping, we will have to delay the showcasing of that one until next time.

That’s all for this update! We’re really happy with the progress so far, and even more excited about what’s coming next. As always, your support and feedback mean the world to us, it helps shape the game and keeps us motivated to make it the best it can be.
If you’re enjoying these devblogs, don’t forget to follow us on X @FoureXo_Games for more updates, sneak peeks, and maybe even the occasional cursed bug GIF.
Thanks for reading, and see you in the next one!

notes.title: Devblog
notes.content:
[b]Hey everyone![/b]
We’re excited to kick off our very first devblog here on Steam! As we continue developing Survivor of [b]Egypt: The Ancient Curse[/b], we want to bring you along for the journey, sharing behind-the-scenes insights, development progress, and sneak peeks at what’s coming next.
In this first post, we’ll talk about where we are in development and give you a glimpse of what’s ahead. Stay tuned, and let’s build something amazing together!

Right now, we’ve built a solid foundation, and the core gameplay is in a great place! With various meta progressions and difficulty scaling, there’s already plenty of replayability. However, one of our biggest challenges at the moment is the beginning of the game. We've noticed that it can be a bit difficult to grasp at first, so we’re focusing on improving onboarding and early-game clarity to make sure new players can jump in and have fun right away.

At the same time, we’re constantly working on improving the look and feel of the game. We believe that great gameplay is even better when supported by equally strong visuals and sound design. Whether it’s refining animations, adding satisfying audio feedback, or enhancing the overall atmosphere, we want every moment to feel immersive and engaging.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45354938/2cf0d5482d5284dfa0bb25093a0176c4dec076e0.png[/img]

[b]What’s Next?[/b]
In the short term, we’re focusing on revamping the class system to make it feel more rewarding and immersive. This includes reworking existing classes and introducing new ones to add more variety and depth to gameplay. Here is a work in progress screenshot of the current class selection for you!

Looking further ahead, we’re planning a brand-new game mode designed for players who want to keep grinding after finishing the main story. While we’re still in the early stages of planning, our goal is to create an engaging endgame experience with plenty of challenges and replayability.

We’ll be sharing more updates as development progresses, and we’d love to hear your thoughts! If you want to stay up to date with the latest news, behind-the-scenes insights, and sneak peeks, be sure to follow us on Twitter [b]@FoureXo_Games[/b]

Your feedback means a lot to us, so feel free to join the conversation and let’s make this game the best it can be together!
